text:
maria: heads up - we're seeing a spike in Pending pods on gpu-nodepools in us-west-2 since last deploy. lots of small GPU jobs can't schedule, looks like severe fragmentation. anyone else seeing this?
aj: saw it this morning, repro with a batch of 4x small-model pods (request 1 gpu, 2 cpu each) - scheduler keeps saying Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu on some nodes even though GPUs are free. :confused:
devon: can you paste the `kubectl describe` output for one pending pod? curious whether it's nodeSelector/nodeAffinity or pure resource shortage.
maria: pasted below - root cause looks like mix of H100 and A100 nodepools, nodeSelector on model-serving images selects h100 which is scarce, but other pods without selector land on A100 nodes leaving 1 GPU unused per node due to cpu/memory fragmentation:
```
Name:           model-a-7f9c5
Namespace:      inference
Status:         Pending
Labels:         app=model-a
Annotations:    <none>
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match node selector, 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 3 Insufficient cpu.
```
leo: that pattern matches fragmentation: some nodes have leftover GPU but not enough CPU for the pod request. we already run system daemons and infra reservations that consume CPUs on gpu nodes.
aj: infra-bot, can you share current node-level allocatable and pods-per-node histograms for the gpu pools?
infra-bot: generating snapshot... will post shortly.
infra-bot: snapshot: us-west-2/gpu-h100-pool: 12 nodes, avg free gpu=0.3, avg free cpu=1.2. us-west-2/gpu-a100-pool: 18 nodes, avg free gpu=0.8, avg free cpu=0.6. High variance across nodes.
devon: two obvious levers: 1) make GPU requests=limits and use integer gpu requests (already), 2) tighten cpu requests on small-model pods so they can pack together. can we set a PodPreset or mutating webhook to reduce conservative requests?
maria: requests already equal limits for gpuresource but CPU requests are overprovisioned by builders. changing all pod specs is a bit of work. any autoscaler tweaks we can try first?
leo: cluster-autoscaler is currently conservative because scale-up is disabled for some pools and mixed-instance-groups cause CA to mis-evaluate. also CA won't scale if Pods have nodeSelector for gpuType that has no matching nodepool capacity.
aj: could we add a small "gpu-pack" nodepool with identical GPU type (H100) and lower CPU/ram flavors so many small pods pack on same nodes? or use binpacking labels + PodAffinity to pack small pods?
devon: pack pool idea is good. alternatively, use resourceTopologyAwareScheduling plugin, or enable the scheduler's topology spread to prefer packing onto fewer nodes (we want binpack, not spread). note: topology spread tends to spread by default so we need custom affinity.
maria: quick mitigation: I can cordon a few A100 nodes and drain big model pods to free up contiguous GPU nodes for small jobs, but that's disruptive.
leo: longer term: create 2 node sizes per gpu type: "gpu-dense-small" (8cpu/64gb per GPU) and "gpu-large" (32cpu/256gb per GPU). promote small jobs to dense pool via label selector. CA autoscaling policies can then keep dense pool right-sized.
aj: also consider enabling binpacking admission webhook that rewrites pod requests? riskier.
devon: another low-risk tweak: reduce kube-reserved/eviction thresholds that are blocking pod placement on near-full nodes? but careful with stability.
maria: any objections if I spin up a 4-node h100-dense pool as a canary and update deployment annotations to target it for the most latency-sensitive small models?
leo: go for it, monitor latency and eviction rates. add a job to simulate spike so we can measure packing efficiency.
infra-bot: action items created: #4367 create h100-dense nodepool (4 nodes), #4368 add label selector docs + quickstart for dev teams, #4369 collect pod packing SLO experiment.
aj: one more thing - remind teams to set topologyAwareHints in the future; also we should document that GPU is integer-only resource and fractional packing requires cpu/mem tuning.
maria: thanks all — starting the nodepool now. will post update in ~30m. :rocket:
